source.usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: Single PDF combines the question paper (printed pages '1 of 14'-'14 of 14' = physical PDF pages 1-14) and a 'DRAFT MARKING SCHEME - MATHEMATICS' (printed 'Page 1 of 10'-'Page 10 of 10' = physical PDF pages 15-24); 'page' below is the physical PDF page of the English question text. Found via https://cisce.org/specimen-question-papers-icse-class-x-2027/ (specimen for the ICSE 2027 examination; examYear=2027 accordingly). Paper prints 'Maximum Marks: 80', 'Time allowed: Three hours', and instruction 'Attempt all questions from Section A and any four questions from Section B.' Section A (40 marks, compulsory) = Q1 (15 objective sub-parts, 1 mark each, MCQ/assertion-reason, split as number '1' part '(i)'.. '(xv)') + Q2 (3 sub-parts, 4 marks each) + Q3 (3 sub-parts: 4, 4, 5 marks). Section B (40 marks) offers Questions 4-10, each worth 10 marks split 3+3+4 across its (i)/(ii)/(iii) sub-parts, candidate attempts any 4 of the 7; the paper prints NO 'OR' alternatives anywhere (no internal-choice pairs), so choiceGroup is null throughout and each (i)/(ii)/(iii) sub-part is its own entry (they are on unrelated syllabus topics and are marked separately); the (a)/(b)/(c) items inside a sub-part are kept together in one entry's text because they share one scenario/date set and cannot be answered stand-alone. Cognitive-level tags printed in the margin (e.g. '[Application]', '[Understanding & Evaluation]') were extracted as floating text and re-attached to their sub-part by position/adjacency in the layout- and raw-mode text; two sub-parts (Q5(iii) and, arguably, one occurrence for Q10(ii)) had no tag reliably attributable and are left without a cognitiveLevel field. IMPORTANT EXTRACTION DEFECT: the PDF's equation-editor text uses a broken font/CMap - italic single-letter variables (x, p, a, b, r, n, y, z, v, w, theta) are simply doubled (each glyph drawn/mapped twice) and were safely de-duplicated, but multi-letter runs (trigonometric function names sin/cos/tan/cot/sec, and ordinary prose words typed via the same equation fields, e.g. 'Interest', 'Slope', 'radius') collapse so that EVERY letter in the run maps to the SAME repeated Unicode character - the actual letters are not recoverable from the text layer at all. Where this affects a value-bearing term (chiefly the trig identity in Q4(iii) and the assertion/reason in Q1(xiii)) the function names were inferred purely from mathematical necessity (the stated identity/result being true) and flagged LOW confidence; where it only affected connective prose in the marking scheme, the wording was reconstructed conservatively from context (flagged MEDIUM) or trimmed with '...'. Matrix questions (Q1(vii), Q4(ii)) print matrix brackets as undecodable glyphs in the text layer; both were reconstructed as row/column notation and cross-checked against the marking scheme's own arithmetic, which matched exactly, but are still flagged MEDIUM per the notation rule. The paper itself prints 'A finite Geometric Proportion (G.P.) series' in Q10(i) (apparently a paper typo for 'Progression'); reproduced verbatim, not corrected. Figures/graphs referenced as 'given figure/diagram' are not reproduced anywhere; question text for such items is otherwise reproduced in full. Two constructions (Q6(iii)) and the ogive/histogram graph questions (Q9(i), Q10(iii)) have marking-scheme content that is itself a hand-drawn diagram/graph in the PDF and did not extract as text; officialAnswer is omitted or trimmed to the one line of text that did extract, as noted per question.

A line is formed joining the two points P(−4, 1) and Q(11, −2). Straight line PQ intersects the x-axis at R. Find the:
(a) ratio PR : RQ.
(b) coordinates of the point R.
(c) equation of the line perpendicular to PQ at R.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) R(x,0), m(−2)+n(1)=0 → −2m+n=0 → m:n = 1:2
∴ PR:RQ = 1:2
(b) x = [1(11)+2(−4)]/(1+2) = 1, R(1, 0)
(c) slope of PQ = (−2−1)/(11+4) = −1/5
slope of line perpendicular to PQ = 5 (reconstructed from context; the descriptive phrase itself is unrecoverable from the text layer)
y − 0 = 5(x − 1)
5x − y = 5

questions.text: A shopkeeper marked an article at ₹ 2000. The rate of GST on the article is 18%. The customer has only ₹ 1888 with him and he requests the shopkeeper to reduce the price so that he can buy the article at ₹ 1888 including GST. What percent discount must the shopkeeper give to do so?

officialAnswer.text:
Let the reduced price be x
x + 18% of x = 1888 → x = ₹ 1600
Reduction in price = ₹ 2000 − ₹1600 = ₹400
Percentage reduction = (400 × 100)/2000 = 20%

questions.text:
Prove the following trigonometric identity:
cos²θ/(1 − tanθ) + sin²θ/(1 − cotθ) = 1 + cosθ sinθ

officialAnswer.text: LHS = cos²θ/(1−tanθ) + sin²θ/(1−cotθ) = cos³θ/(cosθ−sinθ) + sin³θ/(sinθ−cosθ) = (cos³θ−sin³θ)/(cosθ−sinθ) = (cosθ−sinθ)(cos²θ+sin²θ+cosθsinθ)/(cosθ−sinθ) = 1 + cosθsinθ = RHS

questions.text:
Ms. Kaur invested ₹ 8000 in buying ₹ 100 shares of a company paying 6% dividend at ₹ 80. After a year, she sold these shares at ₹ 75 each and invested the proceeds including the dividend received during the first year in buying ₹ 20 shares paying 15% dividend at ₹ 27 each. Find the:
(a) dividend received by her during the first year.
(b) number of shares she purchased using the total proceeds including the dividend.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) No. of shares = 8000/80 = 100
Dividend = (6×100×100)/100 = ₹600
(b) Sale proceeds = ₹75×100 = ₹7500
and Total proceeds = ₹7500 + ₹600 = ₹8100
No. of shares = 8100/27 = 300

questions.text: In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle and AB = AC. If ∠BAC = 32°, find the angles x, y, z, v and w.

officialAnswer.text:
∠BCA = 90° (∠ in a semi-circle) ∴ x + 90° + 32° = 180°, x = 58°
y = x = 58° (angles in the same segment)
z = x = 58° (∠s of the same segment)
AB = AC (given) ∴ ∠ABC = ∠ACB = z = 58°
v + z + z = 180° → v = 180°−116° = 64°
v + w = 180° (opp. ∠s of cyclic quad. and semicircle)
w = 180° − 64° = 116°

questions.text:
In the given diagram, AD ∥ GE ∥ BC, DE = 18 cm, EC = 3 cm, AD = 35 cm.
Find:
(a) AF : FC and AG : GB
(b) length of EF
(c) area (trapezium ADEF) : area (Δ EFC)

∴ AF/FC = DE/EC = 18/3 = 6 (B.P.T.)

questions.text:
In the given figure, the parallelogram ABCD circumscribes a circle, touching the circle at P, Q, R and S. Prove that:
(a) AB = BC
(b) diagonals AC and BD bisect each other at right angles.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) AP=AS, BP=BQ, CR=CQ, DR=DS (tangents drawn from an external point are equal)
Adding, (AP+BP)+(CR+DR) = (AS+DS)+(BQ+CQ)
AB+CD = AD+BC
AB+AB = BC+BC (opp. sides of parallelogram are equal)
2AB = 2BC
AB = BC
(b) In quad ABCD, AB = BC = CD = DA
∴ ABCD is a rhombus
∴ AC and BD bisect each other at right angles (diagonals of rhombus)

Given,
(a + 2b + x)/(a − 2b + x) = (a + b)²/(a − b)², a ≠ 0
Using properties of proportion, find the value of x.

Applying C and D,
[(a+2b+x)+(a−2b+x)] / [(a+2b+x)−(a−2b+x)] = [(a+b)²+(a−b)²] / [(a+b)²−(a−b)²]
2(a+x)/4b = 2(a²+b²)/4ab
(a+x)/b = (a²+b²)/(ab)
(a+x) = (a²+b²)/a
x = b²/a (final step reconstructed algebraically to match the printed intermediate lines; not directly legible in the text layer)

questions.text:
Two beakers (drinking glasses) are cylindrical in shape having diameter and height 7 cm and 10 cm respectively. Glass A has hemispherical raised bottom, and glass B has a conical raised bottom of height 3.5 cm. Determine which glass has a greater capacity and calculate the difference in their capacities. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
(Use π = 22/7)

officialAnswer.text:
VA = πr²h − (2/3)πr³ = π×3.5²×10 − (2/3)×π×3.5³
VB = πr²h − (1/3)πr²h' = π×3.5²×10 − (1/3)×π×3.5³
∴ VB > VA
VB − VA = (2/3)πr³ − (1/3)πr²h' = (1/3)×(22/7)×3.5³ = 44.916 ≈ 44.92
Difference in capacity of Glass A and Glass B = 44.92 cm³. Glass B has greater capacity than Glass A.

questions.text: A finite Geometric Proportion (G.P.) series contains 10 terms. The sum of the first three terms is 7 and that of the last three terms is 896. Find the first term and the common ratio.

officialAnswer.text:
Let the terms be a, ar, ar², …, ar⁹
Given, a+ar+ar² = 7 and ar⁷+ar⁸+ar⁹ = 896
(ar⁷+ar⁸+ar⁹)/(a+ar+ar²) = 896/7
ar⁷(1+r+r²)/[a(1+r+r²)] = 128
r⁷ = 128 → r = 2
a(1+2+2²) = 7 → a = 1

(a) length of PB.
(b) radius of the circle.

PA = PB = 9 cm (tangents from the same point)
In ∆OAP, OA/PA = tan30° = 1/√3
radius = OA = 9 × 1/√3 = 3√3 = 3×1.7321 = 5.1963 = 5.2 cm
